title: Acme Medical - POC scoping / commercial guardrails
summary: AE+SE kickoff to scope a 6-week POC for inference on clinical summarization and triage. Discussed success metrics (latency, accuracy, hallucination tolerance), workload sizing (avg tokens per request, queries/day), benchmark plan (latency p50/p95, throughput, regression tests), pilot credits and guardrails (free credits up to $15k, 2-week extension option, procurement path to enterprise contract), and next steps to run a smoke benchmark and share security docs.
next_steps: Marco to run 3 workload baseline tests with sample prompts by 2025-03-20
Jordan to send pilot credit agreement and pricing summary by 2025-03-18
Acme to provide 10 representative prompts and 1k sample records by 2025-03-19
Schedule technical benchmark session week of 2025-03-24 (SE + Acme infra)
Leah to share procurement timeline and PO requirements by 2025-03-21
action_items: Marco Li - run 3 latency/throughput runs on hosted Redwood; deliver CSV of results - due 2025-03-20
Jordan Patel - share pilot terms doc and $15k credits sheet - due 2025-03-18
Priya Sehgal - provide 10 canonical prompts and 1k deidentified records - due 2025-03-19
Omar Aziz - confirm VPC and KMS requirements, provide network contact - due 2025-03-21
Leah Park - outline procurement milestones and contracting gate dates - due 2025-03-21
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-14 16:00 PST | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Priya (Acme Head of ML), Carlos (CTO), Leah (Procurement), Omar (SRE), Emily (PM)

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining; quick around-the-room, i'm Jordan from Redwood inference, ae, and Marco is our se who will run the benchmarks with you.
00:12 Priya: Hi, priya here, head of ml at acme medical. We're looking to scope a pilot for clinical note summarization and triage. Goal is to offload human triage for low-risk cases.
00:25 Carlos: CTO - evaluating latency and integration surface, also curious on dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs.
00:33 Marco: quick clarifying q, priya, are you planning to keep PHI in requests or will you deidentify before sending to the api?
00:40 Priya: good q - we'll deidentify for the pilot but long term need private deployment / vpc. For the poc we want hosted with strong data residency / retention controls.
00:53 Omar: SRE note: we need to know network egress and kpis; ideally no long-lived keys in the app, integrate with our kms.
01:02 Jordan: great, that's useful. High level agenda: define success criteria, size the workload, agree benchmarks, and nail down commercial guardrails - credits, pilot length, path to contract.

01:30 Priya: success criteria from our side - accuracy/precision on triage labels >= 92% on our dev set, hallucination rate < 3% (manual eval), inference latency p95 < 500ms for summary requests, and cost target under $0.02 per request approximated.
01:55 Marco: noted. Are those averages across 512 tokens or less?
02:02 Priya: typical request is 200-400 input tokens and 50-100 generated tokens.
02:09 Marco: ok that helps; we'll size benchmarks around 300 input / 75 output avg.

02:25 Carlos: scope of pilot - 6 weeks preferred, first 2 weeks integration + smoke tests, next 2 weeks load/bench, final 2 weeks user acceptance and quality evals. Does that align with how redwood typically runs pilots?
02:40 Jordan: yes, 6 weeks is standard. For commercial guardrails we typically offer pilot credits - for this size we can commit $15k of credits on hosted API, with an option to request a 2-week extension and an escalated path to a paid dedicated trial if benchmarks show promise.
02:58 Leah: procurement will need a one-page pilot statement of work and an acceptance criteria doc to sign off. Also need to know billing contact and PO requirements if we convert to paid.
03:10 Jordan: we'll send a pilot SoW and credit agreement and include acceptance criteria you just gave. The credits cover API usage only, not on-prem infra. If you require a dedicated environment we can propose a paid dedicated trial.

03:30 Marco: technical benchmark plan - we'll run three standard tests: 1) latency microbench: single-request latency for 1000 samples, measure p50/p95/p99; 2) throughput run: ramp to target qps (we estimate 100 qps peak for you) for 10 minutes; 3) regression eval: run your 1k sample set for quality metrics and hallucination checks. We'll provide scripts and a results CSV.
03:56 Priya: 100 qps peak is approx what we'd see in production? looks high for triage but ok for stress. Our normal steady state is 20-30 qps.
04:08 Marco: thanks, we'll test both 30 qps steady and a 100 qps spike. Also will test with batched requests to understand cost/latency tradeoffs.

04:30 Omar: about security - we require SOC2 type II, audit logs, SSO via SAML, RBAC for keys, and ability to integrate with our Azure Key Vault or bring-your-own-kms. What can you provide on hosted?
04:45 Jordan: Redwood hosted environment is SOC2 compliant, we provide audit logs, SSO/SAML, and KMS integrations; we will share the security pack. For private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and VPC.
04:59 Omar: good to know. Also need data retention to be configurable - we can't have logs beyond 30 days for the pilot.
05:08 Jordan: we can set retention to 30 days for pilot logs; we'll put that in the SoW.

05:20 Marco: on models - we'll test with open variants you suggested, and a quantized variant for cost comparison. For latency goals under 500ms p95 on hosted, we expect to hit that on optimized kernels for 4k context models but will confirm.
05:36 Priya: is there a fallback plan if latency is too high? we can't degrade user experience.
05:41 Marco: yes - routing policies: you can prefer lower-latency model variants or enable cached prefixes for repeated templates. For strict latency we can move to dedicated GPU capacity as next step.

06:00 Carlos: commercial question - what are the terms of the credits: expiry, usage caps, and what happens after credits are consumed?
06:10 Jordan: credits expire 60 days from issuance for pilots. Usage caps we can set per project; after credits consumed, you can convert to pay-as-you-go invoiced monthly or transition to reserved dedicated capacity via contract. We'll include pricing bands in the sheet.
06:23 Leah: procurement will want an explicit conversion path and a target contract value estimate for budgeting. Can you provide a rough annualized number if we move to reserved capacity to handle 100 qps?
06:35 Jordan: rough back-of-envelope: for 100 qps steady and your token sizes, we'd estimate order-of-magnitude $X/month - we'll run a cost model; Marco will include cost estimates per run in the CSV.
06:49 Marco: yes i'll include three scenarios: hosted payg, hosted with batching, and dedicated reserved with percent commit.

07:10 Priya: acceptance testing - we want an A/B pass/fail set: 1) triage accuracy >= 92% on held-out set, 2) hallucination manual spot-check below threshold, 3) latency p95 < 500ms for 75 token output. If these are met we move to procurement.
07:28 Jordan: noted, we'll mirror those acceptance criteria in the SoW.

07:40 Emily: what's the procurement timeline? we need legal review and a security questionnaire.
07:46 Leah: procurement target is to complete contract in 6-8 weeks after successful pilot, but we need visibility on vendor SSO, PIAs, and SOC2.
07:58 Jordan: we'll provide security docs and a standard MSA; if you need custom terms we'll surface to our legal ops.

08:12 Marco: operationally, for the smoke run we need 10 canonical prompts and 1k deidentified records. Please deliver them to marco@redwood.com SFTP or secure share. We'll also need a contact for your infra to coordinate network allowlist.
08:27 Priya: i'll get that to you, we prefer sftp.

08:35 Jordan: quick note on guardrails: pilot credits exclude on-prem deployment effort; any dedicated infra incurs separate charges. We'll also include a 2-week extension clause in the credit agreement to cover unexpected delays.
08:49 Leah: that extension option is helpful. Also we may request a cap on overages if we spike.
08:55 Jordan: we can add an overage cap and notification threshold.

09:05 Marco: timeline recap - send SoW + credits by Tue 2025-03-18; acme to provide data by Wed 2025-03-19; se to run initial smoke by Thu 2025-03-20; schedule full benchmark w/c 2025-03-24.
09:22 Priya: sounds good.

09:30 Jordan: any last open items?
09:33 Carlos: just clarify model licensing for clinical use - are there restrictions?
09:38 Marco: we'll check model terms; most open variants are permissive, but some weights have usage constraints - i'll flag any issues.
09:48 Priya: also, we may want an NDA addendum for the data share.
09:52 Jordan: we can do that, leah, add to your procurement notes.

10:00 Jordan: thanks everyone, recap will be in email: SoW + pilot credit doc + security pack + scheduling link. Next call: technical benchmark session week of 3/24.
10:10 Leah: thanks all.
10:13 Meeting ended.
